UG ProgrammeWhy It Matters.Why It Matters.The Content Creator Challenge (CCC) is a hands-on course that students take in their second year to learn the art and business of content creation. In today's digital economy where attention is currency and influence drives buying decisions, CCC gives students a sharp edge in building personal brands and mastering platform-first strategies.Core focus of the course is influencer marketing, now central to how brands connect with audiences. India stands at the cusp of a multi-sectoral transformation driven by shifting consumer preferences, national security imperatives, and a green energy transition. This report highlights three sectors that are central to shaping the country's economic and strategic future: Consumer, Defence & Shipbuilding, and Renewable Energy.The Indian consumer economy continues to be one of the most resilient and fastest-growing globally. With rising disposable incomes, a young and aspirational demographic, and accelerating digital adoption, consumption-led growth is expanding beyond metros into Tier 2 and 3 towns. Premiumization, D2C channels, and category innovation (across beauty, personal care, athleisure, etc.) are redefining demand patterns. While global macro conditions remain volatile, domestic consumption is expected to drive long-term growth, aided by formalization, credit access, and rapid infrastructure development.India's Defence & Shipbuilding sector is undergoing a structural overhaul under the "Make in India" and "Atmanirbhar Bharat" missions. Defence production is being indigenized at scale, with exports rising nearly 34-fold over the past decade. Policies like DAP 2020, defence corridors, corporatization of ordnance factories, and MSME/startup involvement through iDEX are enabling private and public sector synergies. In naval shipbuilding, India has developed the capability to build advanced warships, including nuclear submarines and aircraft carriers. However, commercial shipbuilding remains underpenetrated. Structural challenges in financing, infrastructure, and global competitiveness persist, but recent incentives and a ₹25,000 crore maritime development fund signal a strategic push to revive the sector.In Renewable Energy, India has emerged as the third-largest market globally, with 203 GW installed capacity and an ambitious target of 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.

Structural challenges in financing, infrastructure, and global competitiveness persist, but recent incentives and a ₹25,000 crore maritime development fund signal a strategic push to revive the sector.In Renewable Energy, India has emerged as the third-largest market globally, with 203 GW installed capacity and an ambitious target of 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. Programs like the PLI scheme for solar and batteries, the Green Hydrogen Mission, and viability gap funding for offshore wind are accelerating this shift. However, coal still accounts for ~72% of actual generation, raising questions about whether the transition is truly green or merely compensating for rising demand. A stronger storage infrastructure, transmission buildout, and regulatory support are key to enabling renewables to displace fossil fuels at scale.Together, these sectors reflect India's pivot towards self-reliance, climate action, and consumption-led growth.

Indian shipbuilders face a substantial cost disadvantage in financing. Interest rates in India have been higher than in East Asia, and crucially, ships do not qualify as "infrastructure" assets for loans. As Sanjeev Sanyal highlights, ships are not included in India's Harmonized List of Infrastructure, meaning shipbuilding projects cannot access the long-term, low-interest financing available to other infrastructure sectors. This exclusion also means banks cannot easily accept ships as collateral, because under India's SARFAESI Act (Section 31(d)), vessels are not covered banks can't seize and auction a ship as security if a loan defaults. Without reform (adding ships to infra category and amending laws), this will continue to hinder growth.Lack of Scale and Infrastructure: Most Indian shipyards are small with limited dock capacity and outdated infrastructure. With rising demand, growing climate risks, and a net-zero target by 2070, renewable energy has moved from the margins to the center of India's policy agenda. The government aims to install 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, positioning India as a key player in the global clean energy transition.Yet, the picture is mixed. While solar and wind capacity have grown rapidly, coal still accounts for about threequarters of India's power generation45, and coal use hit record highs even in 2024. This contrast has sparked debate: is India's energy transition real, or is it selective greenwashing?IntroductionIndia is rapidly scaling up renewable energy as part of its economic and climate strategy. It has committed to installing 500 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030, including solar, wind, hydro, and nuclear a goal announced at COP26 and aligned with India's target of sourcing 50% of electricity from non-fossil sources by 2030. Achieving this requires ~50 GW of new additions annually through 2030 nearly double the ~27.9 GW added in 2024. As of late 2024, India has crossed 203 GW of renewable capacity, accounting for about 46% of total power capacity46.This report examines that question through a data-driven lens. It begins with a look at India's energy mix evolution, followed by a critical assessment of the green transition versus greenwashing. It then explores the EPC boom, equity market activity including recent IPOs, and trends in startup investments offering investors and policymakers a comprehensive view of India's renewable energy landscape.This clean energy push is driven by energy security, climate leadership, and domestic development.

In 2010, coal accounted for roughly 70% of generation and the balance was mostly conventional hydro and gas. By 2022, coal's share in generation was about 72%, with renewables (wind, solar, hydro, bio) contributing most of the remaining 28%. Yet simultaneously, India is expanding coal mining and considering new coal power plants.Green Transition or Greenwashing?50Continued coal investments: Despite official statements about not requiring new coal beyond projects already under construction, recent developments indicate a revival of coal expansion. In 2023, India went on a coal plant permitting spree, approving or moving forward nearly 11.5 GW of new coal power projects (3.9 GW permitted and 7.6 GW given early-stage clearances in just the first half of 2023)53. Moreover, the government is planning to ramp up coal production to 1 billion tonnes by opening new mines to avoid future supply shortages.

Moreover, the government is planning to ramp up coal production to 1 billion tonnes by opening new mines to avoid future supply shortages. In total, around 50 GW of new coal plants could come online by 2030, even as renewables surge.The rationale given by Indian authorities is energy security and reliability. In the face of soaring power demand (India saw record peak demand in 2022 and 2023) and renewable project delays, officials turned to coal as a "quick fix" for avoiding blackouts54. For example, the Power Ministry in 2023 directed utilities to operate old coal plants at full capacity during summer and even import coal as needed. This short-term pivot to coal reflects legitimate concerns renewables, being intermittent, cannot yet single-handedly meet peaks without adequate storage and grid upgrades. However, it also reveals that the green transition is not (yet) displacing coal instead, coal usage is increasing in absolute terms alongside renewables.Figure 17: Source: IndiaDataInsightsStranded asset risk: Expanding coal capacity now carries significant financial risk over the plant lifetime. Here India faces challenges. The country's grid, while improving, needs massive expansion and upgrades to handle the targeted 500 GW of non-fossil capacity. The government has approved a ₹2.44 lakh crore (~$30 bn) transmission plan for integrating 500 GW by 2030, including new high-voltage corridors and grid-scale battery stations. Energy storage is still nascent India has just a few hundred MW of battery storage commissioned, though tenders for 4,000 MWh of battery storage were floated in 2022-23 and plans are afoot for pump hydro storage projects. Without adequate storage, renewable energy can lead to curtailment (unused excess power) or instability when penetration gets high. The evolution of advanced technologies, such as artificial intelli-gence, space communications, bio-manufacturing, and adaptive organic chemistry, further complicates collaboration. Yet, these technologies, like AI, also enhance the effectiveness of these collaborations by streamlining processes and improving both educa-tional outcomes and corporate performance. This is particularly relevant in the context of Industry 4.0, where the synergy between academia and industry is essential for developing a skilled workforce capa-ble of adapting to rapid technological changes. As industries shift and technological advancements accelerate, a dynamic and responsive education sys-tem is essential to equip students with a combina-tion of theoretical knowledge, practical skills, and an adaptive learning mindset required to meet the demands of the modern workforce.Education and industry: The traditional model of edu-cation, which often emphasises theoretical knowl-edge, is no longer sufficient to meet the demands of modern industries. Industries are now increas-ingly looking for candidates who possess not just academic credentials but also the ability to apply their knowledge in real-world scenarios. This shift has led to a growing recognition of the importance of integrating industry-relevant skills into educa-tional curricula.Furthermore, the traditional approach that four years of training will prepare someone for forty years of work is losing validity. Industry-academia collaborations are emerging as a solution to this challenge, offering a platform for the co-evolution of learning systems.

With rising disposable incomes, a young and aspirational demographic, and accelerating digital adoption, consumption-led growth is expanding beyond metros into Tier 2 and 3 towns. Premiumization, D2C channels, and category innovation (across beauty, personal care, athleisure, etc.) are redefining demand patterns. While global macro conditions remain volatile, domestic consumption is expected to drive long-term growth, aided by formalization, credit access, and rapid infrastructure development.India's Defence & Shipbuilding sector is undergoing a structural overhaul under the "Make in India" and "Atmanirbhar Bharat" missions. Defence production is being indigenized at scale, with exports rising nearly 34-fold over the past decade. Policies like DAP 2020, defence corridors, corporatization of ordnance factories, and MSME/startup involvement through iDEX are enabling private and public sector synergies. Structural challenges in financing, infrastructure, and global competitiveness persist, but recent incentives and a ₹25,000 crore maritime development fund signal a strategic push to revive the sector.In Renewable Energy, India has emerged as the third-largest market globally, with 203 GW installed capacity and an ambitious target of 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. Programs like the PLI scheme for solar and batteries, the Green Hydrogen Mission, and viability gap funding for offshore wind are accelerating this shift. This report provides a cross-country perspective on India's consumer evolution, benchmarking it against China, Japan, and South Korea across key sub-sectors: retail, e-commerce, FMCG, luxury, and financial services.We begin by outlining macroeconomic and demographic drivers of consumer demand urbanization, income growth, digital penetration, and population dynamics before comparing sector-specific developments. Data from credible sources is cited throughout, with charts and benchmarks used to highlight India's positioning relative to its peers.India was the fastest-growing major economy in this period, with real GDP growth averaging ~6 7% annually. Japan, in contrast, saw stagnant or declining nominal incomes GDP per head fell from ~$38,500 in 2014 to ~$34,000 in 2022 (partly due to currency depreciation)1 reflecting its slow-growth, deflationary environment. Analysts and industry stakeholders point to several key challenges:In essence, India's shipbuilding sector has been held back by a combination of financial, structural, and policy challenges. However, awareness of these hurdles is high, and recent measures are targeted at addressing them. The next section discusses how the government is directly tackling many of these pain points to turn shipbuilding into a growth industry.Key Challenges and Constraints to shipbuildingFinancing and Cost of Capital: Shipbuilding is highly capital-intensive setting up modern docks, cranes, and fabrication infrastructure costs hundreds of millions of dollars, and building large ships ties up capital for long durations. Indian shipbuilders face a substantial cost disadvantage in financing. Interest rates in India have been higher than in East Asia, and crucially, ships do not qualify as "infrastructure" assets for loans. As Sanjeev Sanyal highlights, ships are not included in India's Harmonized List of Infrastructure, meaning shipbuilding projects cannot access the long-term, low-interest financing available to other infrastructure sectors. This exclusion also means banks cannot easily accept ships as collateral, because under India's SARFAESI Act (Section 31(d)), vessels are not covered banks can't seize and auction a ship as security if a loan defaults. Without reform (adding ships to infra category and amending laws), this will continue to hinder growth.Lack of Scale and Infrastructure: Most Indian shipyards are small with limited dock capacity and outdated infrastructure.

Without reform (adding ships to infra category and amending laws), this will continue to hinder growth.Lack of Scale and Infrastructure: Most Indian shipyards are small with limited dock capacity and outdated infrastructure. In contrast, Chinese and Korean yards boast dozens of docks and a robust local supplier ecosystem. Indian yards often import key components, which inflates costs, and lack the automation (e.g. welding robots) needed for competitive efficiency.High Operating Costs: While labor is inexpensive, productivity is hampered by skill gaps and outdated processes. Indian yards have also struggled with cost overruns and delivery delays, especially on first-time projects.Global Competition and Cyclicality: Shipbuilding demand is tied to global trade cycles. Indian yards were hit hard by the post-2008 downturn. Though India introduced a 20% shipbuilding subsidy in 2016, slow implementation limited its impact though recent extensions may help.Policy and Regulatory Delays: The absence of a central shipbuilding authority with roles split across ministries led to intermittent policy support. For example, a key subsidy was withdrawn in 2007 just before the global crash, and calls to grant ships infrastructure status remain unimplemented despite repeated committee recommendations.The Indian government has in recent years launched a comprehensive effort to revive and expand shipbuilding, recognizing it as both an economic multiplier and a strategic necessity. With rising demand, growing climate risks, and a net-zero target by 2070, renewable energy has moved from the margins to the center of India's policy agenda. The government aims to install 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, positioning India as a key player in the global clean energy transition.Yet, the picture is mixed. While solar and wind capacity have grown rapidly, coal still accounts for about threequarters of India's power generation45, and coal use hit record highs even in 2024. This contrast has sparked debate: is India's energy transition real, or is it selective greenwashing?IntroductionIndia is rapidly scaling up renewable energy as part of its economic and climate strategy. It has committed to installing 500 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030, including solar, wind, hydro, and nuclear a goal announced at COP26 and aligned with India's target of sourcing 50% of electricity from non-fossil sources by 2030. Achieving this requires ~50 GW of new additions annually through 2030 nearly double the ~27.9 GW added in 2024. As of late 2024, India has crossed 203 GW of renewable capacity, accounting for about 46% of total power capacity46.This report examines that question through a data-driven lens. It begins with a look at India's energy mix evolution, followed by a critical assessment of the green transition versus greenwashing. It then explores the EPC boom, equity market activity including recent IPOs, and trends in startup investments offering investors and policymakers a comprehensive view of India's renewable energy landscape.This clean energy push is driven by energy security, climate leadership, and domestic development.

In the face of soaring power demand (India saw record peak demand in 2022 and 2023) and renewable project delays, officials turned to coal as a "quick fix" for avoiding blackouts54. For example, the Power Ministry in 2023 directed utilities to operate old coal plants at full capacity during summer and even import coal as needed. This short-term pivot to coal reflects legitimate concerns renewables, being intermittent, cannot yet single-handedly meet peaks without adequate storage and grid upgrades. Here India faces challenges. The country's grid, while improving, needs massive expansion and upgrades to handle the targeted 500 GW of non-fossil capacity. When will students get their application results and get shortlisted for the further round? Results can be expected to be announced anywhere between 15-30 days after the commencement of the deadline. Post receiving information on the shortlist, students will receive an online Scholarship (Aptitude) Test that they have to take online from home. What if a student has submitted the video but didn't get the Scholarship (Aptitude) Test mail yet? The email will be sent once the video is evaluated and students are selected. Results can be expected to be announced anywhere between 15-30 days after the submission of the video. Find more details here. here . What are the passing marks? We look into the profile holistically before selecting or rejecting a student. However, please note that scoring 35 marks (out of a total of 45) is the eligibility criteria for scholarship opportunities. Can students submit their JEE/SAT/CUET Score instead of taking the Masters' Union Scholarship (Aptitude) Test? Yes, students also have the option to provide their JEE/IPMAT/SAT/CUET scores.

However, please note that scoring 35 marks (out of a total of 45) is the eligibility criteria for scholarship opportunities. Can students submit their JEE/SAT/CUET Score instead of taking the Masters' Union Scholarship (Aptitude) Test? Yes, students also have the option to provide their JEE/IPMAT/SAT/CUET scores. The Scholarship (Aptitude) Test becomes optional for those who have provided their scores and they will be shortlisted on the basis of the score. Please note that the scholarship test is not just for students looking for scholarships but is also an essential step of our admission process which enables us to assess the analytical capabilities of the student. Is it mandatory to choose a certification (CA or CFA) or sit for the professional exams? No, the decision to sit for the external professional exams (CA or CFA) is entirely optional. The programme is designed to provide the curriculum and preparation necessary for these pathways. CA (ICAI) and CFA (CFA Institute) are independent, external qualifications. If you pay the registration fee and clear a level of one (e.g., CA Foundation) and then switch to the other (CFA), you will have to start from Level I of the new certification. What is the difference between the Masters' Union certification and the IIM Bangalore degree? The IIM Bangalore (BBA) degree is a traditional academic qualification offered with standard coursework and university examinations. How does the 2+2 structure work? Students study Years 1 and 2 in India and then transfer to Griffith for Years 3 and 4. If you have submitted a CAT or GMAT score and are happy with it, then you are not required to take the MU-BAAT. The MU-BAAT is designed to evaluate: Your communication and business aptitude Clarity of thought and idea structuring Creative and analytical thinking You record your responses online and do not need any prior preparation. Think of the questions as a conversation with the Masters' Union team that helps us understand you beyond your r sum . Duration: 45-60 minutes Format: 9 questions divided into 5 sections. What is the difference between the Flagship PGP TBM program vs the PGP TBM YLC? The content and pedagogy of both PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC remain identical. The PGP TBM Young Leaders Cohort is specifically designed for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience. It follows the same curriculum as the PGP TBM but spans 24 months instead of 16 months. A key highlight of the PGP TBM YLC is a mandatory 3-month internship, offering students practical, real-world exposure to prepare them for leadership roles. Additionally, each core course is taught over 30 hours instead of 20 hours in the PGP TBM. This ensures that students build a strong foundation in critical academic concepts. Are the Scholarships the Same for PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC? Yes, the scholarships available for both the PGP TBM and the PGP TBM YLC are the same. The final grades for most courses will be determined by a mix of class participation, quizzes, simulations, group assignments, projects and exams. Masters' Union grades the exams on a Standard Normal Curve, also called a Z-curve, with a mean of 3.0. There are no forced-to-fails. To graduate, students must maintain a mean grade of 2.1 in both the core and electives courses. What are the benefits of the 16-month programme? The PGP TBM at Masters' Union, with its unique 16-month format, encapsulates the best global practices in management education through a pedagogical approach. Designed to be a fast-paced academic experience, it includes 13 months of rigorous academic training in core areas and industry concentrations with a three-month period of internship and industry immersion, and opportunities to network and seek mentorship. The course is designed for individuals with more than 1 year of work experience.Being in this state of constant engagement gives an opportunity for students to learn how to set priorities and make choices about learning, socialising and personal time from the very beginning of the programme, making them an expert at decision-making, which is one of the most valued qualities in a business leader. What are the benefits of the 24-month PGP TBM YLC programme? The PGP TBM YLC, on the other hand, is specifically crafted for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience and spans 24 months. While the content and pedagogy are identical to the flagship program, the extended timeline allows for deeper learning and gradual development.

If an applicant is from a non-tech background, is the Masters' Union a right fit for them? The world of work is transforming faster than ever. With AI, hybrid teams, and global mobility reshaping organisations, HR has become a core driver of business strategy. India produces ~5 lakh MBAs , yet under 5% specialise in HR , despite growing demand for leaders skilled in analytics, culture, and people strategy. Globally, the CHRO is now the #2 most in-demand C-suite role after CTO , reflecting HR's rising importance. If you have submitted a CAT or GMAT score and are happy with it, then you are not required to take the MU-BAAT. The MU-BAAT is designed to evaluate: Your communication and business aptitude Clarity of thought and idea structuring Creative and analytical thinking You record your responses online and do not need any prior preparation. A 16-month full-time postgraduate programme blending Masters' Union's business foundation with hands-on specialisations in human capital, organisational design, leadership, and people analytics. What will I learn in the Programme?

A 16-month full-time postgraduate programme blending Masters' Union's business foundation with hands-on specialisations in human capital, organisational design, leadership, and people analytics. What will I learn in the Programme? Learn to build people strategies, design organisations, and lead talent in a fast-changing business environment. Learn directly from top faculty, CHROs, CXOs, and founders through live case studies, mentorship, and industry-led workshops. Our "learn by doing" curriculum shapes future HR leaders at the intersection of people, strategy, culture, and analytics. What is the program Structure? The curriculum spans 8 terms across 16 months Terms 1 2 building core business foundations Terms 3 5 mastering human resources & organisation strategy Term 6-8: Capstone and consulting projects with real organisations What will be the batch size of the class? We will limit the batch size to a maximum of 60 students to ensure personalised learning, close mentorship from masters, and a highly effective teacher student ratio. What is the eligibility criteria? The PGP in Human Resources & Organisation Strategy is open to candidates who have completed their undergraduate degree or will graduate by April 2026 onwards. Ideal applicants include fresh graduates, early-career professionals (0 5 years), and professionals aspiring to build careers in people, culture, and organisational leadership. How do I apply? Click Apply Now (tag the application now link) on our website, complete the online application form, and our admissions team will reach out to you at the earliest possible time. Are scholarships available for the PGP HR&OS programme?

How do I apply? Click Apply Now (tag the application now link) on our website, complete the online application form, and our admissions team will reach out to you at the earliest possible time. Are scholarships available for the PGP HR&OS programme? Yes, scholarships are available for candidates with strong leadership potential, prior people management exposure, and demonstrated impact in organisational or HR-related initiatives How can I avail the scholarship? While completing your application, you can express interest in available scholarships. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to submit supporting documents or short essays to confirm their eligibility. If an application has been unsuccessful, may they reapply in the next round? No, candidates cannot reapply in the next round. They may reapply for the next intake in the following academic year by submitting a new online application. It's advisable to do so only if there have been significant updates or improvements to their profile since the previous application. Will I get to network with Industry leaders? Yes, you will learn and engage with top faculties, CHROs, people leaders, founders, and CXOs across diverse industries. Can I work on my own startup ideas during the programme? Absolutely. The programme fosters entrepreneurial thinking and provides ample opportunities to apply classroom and immersion learnings to your own ventures. If you have submitted a CAT or GMAT score and are happy with it, then you are not required to take the MU-BAAT. The MU-BAAT is designed to evaluate: Your communication and business aptitude Clarity of thought and idea structuring Creative and analytical thinking You record your responses online and do not need any prior preparation. Think of the questions as a conversation with the Masters' Union team that helps us understand you beyond your r sum . Duration: 45-60 minutes Format: 9 questions divided into 5 sections. You will receive a link from us typically 1-2 weeks after you submit your application. You will then have 14 days to take the test. Frequently Asked Questions Employment Report Is PGP Rise: General Management equivalent to other Executive MBA Programmes offered in the country? The academic content and rigour of the Masters' Union PGP Rise: General Management are equivalent to other Executive MBA programmes. However, Indian regulations do not allow independent institutions to grant a Master's degree. After completion of the programme, applicants will receive a certificate of completion of the Post Graduate Programme in Management for Senior Professionals. Can applicants continue to work full-time while pursuing the programme? Yes, applicants can continue their full-time job as they pursue PGP Rise: General Management by Masters' Union. What happens when applicants are not in the residency? Their studies will continue on the weekend in a hybrid model where they can choose to attend in-person classes at our Gurgaon campus or join in virtually. What will be the batch size of the class? We will limit the batch size to a maximum of 60 students to maximize individual attention from masters, and have an impactful teacher-student ratio. What are the core emphasis areas of the Masters' Union PGP Rise: General Management curriculum? We offer India's first programme with industry-focused coaching at its core. Students get expert mentorship to define their career goals. They benefit from psychometric assessments and industry-focused coaching, all tailored to meet the following needs of mid-career professionals: Mid-career transition guidance Enhancing your professional brand Interview preparation strategy How many days of leave will an applicant require to participate in the immersive weeks?

If you are dealing with complex family dynamics or need long-term business transformation, leadership growth, and legacy building, OPM is the right choice. It is a 12-month programme for those focused on sustainable growth, succession, and global business exposure. If there are not too many complications in your family dynamics, your primary pain point is sales or business acceleration, and you want to make a shorter commitment of your time, then 9-month BAP is a better program for you. What is the main outcome difference?

It is a 12-month programme for those focused on sustainable growth, succession, and global business exposure. If there are not too many complications in your family dynamics, your primary pain point is sales or business acceleration, and you want to make a shorter commitment of your time, then 9-month BAP is a better program for you. What is the main outcome difference? 12 months OPM = holistic, sustainable transformation and leadership 9 months BAP = fast, practical sales and process gains Will there be the same level of rigour of practical application in both the programs? Yes. Both programs include assignments and Capstone to ensure whatever is taught in the class is thoroughly applied in your company. A pressing problem that your organisation is currently facing is solved with the help of Capstone, with one on one coaching by faculty and mentors. Will I miss out a lot by choosing the BAP? It's all about what your need is. Yes, you will miss out on some aspects like in-depth modules for family, self, patriarch, non family CXOs. Also, international immersions and Fractional Board. Nevertheless, if your current pressing need is revenue growth, then you can go for BAP. Is it worth doing the 12-month program if my goal is only sales growth? It is better to compare all aspects of both programs, what different and additional you are getting in each, and then decide. Can freshers apply for the 9-month BAP Certificate? Not recommended. Both OPM and BAP are designed keeping needs of family business owners and promoters. Is the 9-month BAP course a subset of OPM? No. It is a different program. While some sessions are similar to OPM, there are many sessions in BAP which are not taught in OPM. See Modules Comparison. Can I switch from OPM to BAP? OPM's first batch with generous scholarships, offer of bringing a family member for free, international immersions, Fractional Board, and almost 2X course modules offers incredible value. Hence, we strongly dissuade students from switching from OPM to BAP. Having completed BAP, can I upgrade myself to OPM by doing additional courses and modules? Yes, it is possible by doing additional modules and international immersions. However, we would like to understand your business objectives and then recommend the best way forward. Frequently Asked Questions Employment Report How does the programme's format support family business successors in driving change within their business? The PGP Rise: Owners & Promoters Management is designed so that scions can apply their learnings to the business, in real time after each key module. The classes take place over the weekend, with learners having the option of attending them in person. How does the curriculum address the unique challenges faced by family business owners? The programme addresses the complete spectrum of responsibilities that family business owners must balance family, business, self, and ownership. It also acknowledges the significance of including other key stakeholders in the process by conducting specialised "Extended Learning Sessions" for family members and the leadership team in dedicated residencies. How does the programme implement a hands-on approach to solving business owners' challenges? Alongside academic rigour, the programme encompasses a Capstone Project based on real challenges faced by the learners in their family business.

It also acknowledges the significance of including other key stakeholders in the process by conducting specialised "Extended Learning Sessions" for family members and the leadership team in dedicated residencies. How does the programme implement a hands-on approach to solving business owners' challenges? Alongside academic rigour, the programme encompasses a Capstone Project based on real challenges faced by the learners in their family business. Over the course of 12 intensive months and with the help of 1:1 coaching with industry experts, learners will identify core challenges within the business and drive tangible solutions by the end of the programme. How do international immersions and domestic residencies enhance the learning experience of participants? International immersions and domestic residencies offer a holistic learning experience, exposing learners to both global and local business perspectives. This diverse exposure enables learners to apply insights to their family enterprises, fostering their ability to navigate markets effectively. Through Global University Immersions , participants are exposed to world-class practices and latest research equipping them with the tools to innovate and scale their family businesses internationally.The Industrial Visits allow them to understand global market trends, identify expansion opportunities and gain first-hand exposure to successful business models in international hubs. The Domestic Residencies offer a focused exploration of Indian family businesses, enabling participants to witness approaches that are unique to the Indian business landscape. What will be the batch size of the class? We will limit the batch size to a maximum of 60 students to maximise individual attention from the masters and have an impactful teacher-student ratio. What role does mentorship play in the overall learning experience of the programme? Learners can expect 1:1 mentorship from experienced family business owners, industry titans & consultants, who provide firsthand insights drawn from their experiences in balancing family dynamics with business innovation.

PGP Bharat is a 6-month immersion-led programme where India becomes your classroom combining travel, business and cultural immersions, In Class and Out Class experiences, and hands-on learning. How many cities and immersions does the programme cover? Students travel across 20+ cities (list of cities can be found in the brochure and website) and engage in 40+ immersive experiences covering industries, enterprises, and cultural sites. Is PGP Bharat an MBA equivalent? PGP Bharat is a Post Graduate Programme (PGP) that emphasizes experiential learning in business education. While not an MBA, it offers one-of-its-kind business exposure and practical learning that no other course in the country currently provides. Will I get a degree after completing PGP Bharat? You will receive a Post Graduate Programme (PGP) certification, similar to the PGP-TBM offered at Masters' Union. What will I learn in the programme? Through industry immersions, CXO interactions, and cultural experiences, you'll gain real-world exposure to how business works in India.

Will I get a degree after completing PGP Bharat? You will receive a Post Graduate Programme (PGP) certification, similar to the PGP-TBM offered at Masters' Union. What will I learn in the programme? Through industry immersions, CXO interactions, and cultural experiences, you'll gain real-world exposure to how business works in India. You'll shape your digital identity in the Creator Challenge, build hands-on skills by launching ventures in the Venture Initiation Programme, and hone your entrepreneurial skills through the Dropshipping Challenge. Alongside, you'll master business fundamentals across strategy, finance, marketing, and technology while developing the perspective and self-awareness to grow as a future leader. What is the programme structure? Term 0: Orientation at Gurugram Campus Term 1: Travel-based Immersions & Creator Challenge as Out Class Term 2: Dropshipping Challenge as Out Class & In Class sessions Term 3: Venture Initiation Programme & In Class sessions What is the eligibility criteria? PGP Bharat is open to all candidates who have completed their undergraduate degree or are graduating in April 2026 onwards. Do I need prior work experience? No prior work experience is required. The programme is designed for learners at different stages of their journey, but it is especially recommended for those with a strong interest in business, travel, and experiential learning. How do I apply? Click Apply Now on our website, fill out the online application form, and start your transformative journey across India. Are scholarships available for PGP Bharat? Can I work on my own startup ideas during the programme? Absolutely. Will I get cultural exposure while learning business? Yes, cultural immersions are integrated at every city stop, including heritage sites, local communities, and regional business practices. Bharat Fellowship is a 6 week immersion-led programme that uses India as the classroom, combining travel with business and cultural immersions, and one day challenges for hands-on learning. How many cities and immersions does the programme cover? Students travel across 10+ cities and engage in 25+ immersive experiences covering industries, enterprises and cultural sites. What is a fellowship? Bharat Fellowship is an immersion-led learning programme that offers participants structured experiential exposure through travel across India, business and cultural immersions and hands-on projects in the form of One Day Challenges. Will I get a degree after completing Bharat Fellowship? You will receive a fellowship certification. What will I learn in the programme? Through industry immersions, CXO interactions, and cultural experiences, you will gain first-hand exposure to how businesses operate across India. You can build a digital identity through Content Creation and sharpen entrepreneurial thinking through the One Day Challenges. What is the programme structure? A Master is an individual who is or has been a distinguished authority or global expert in his/her area of occupation, and has made positive and significant contributions to the world of business and society. A Master is typically a top industry practitioner, an eminent businessman, a veteran public leader or politician, a renowned civil servant, a public institution head, a global technologist, a civil society changemaker, a member of the armed forces or a distinguished academic. You can get involved with Masters' Union in one or more of the following ways: The CXO Shadow Program: As a CXO, one or two students get the unique opportunity to shadow you at your work environment, over a stretch of time, and observe what being an industry leader entails on a daily basis. The student(s) get to experience firsthand how the industry leadership makes critical business decisions and works towards realising the visions of their respective organizations. Master Mentor: As a Master Mentor, you can stay engaged with a group(s) of students through a range of activities that enhance their educational experience, including but not limited to conducting masterclasses and storytelling sessions, sharing personal industry experience, providing professional guidance, knowledge, advice, career opportunities and resources to achieve specific goals underlying the student-mentor relationships at Masters' Union. Research Mentor at our Research Centers: As a Research Mentor at one of our state-of-the-art research centers, you mentor the young researchers and students of the Union to conduct cutting-edge research, while also identifying and crafting novel business applications using the research findings that emerge from them. At Masters' Union we believe that financial constraints should not pose any hindrance to students' academic aspirations. We have merit and need-based scholarships for all deserving candidates. Students scoring above 35 out of 45 marks in the Masters' Union Scholarship Aptitude test get a scholarship which can range from 10% - 25% of the tuition fee depending on the student's performance in the Scholarship (Aptitude)Test and the overall profile of the applicant. For candidates keen on scholarship, we encourage students to submit their application early to allow for our admission counsellors to thoroughly review their scholarship case before presenting it to the admissions committee at the time of evaluation. Is the scholarship for all four years or just for the first year? Scholarship is awarded for all four years. However, students nominated and admitted to Illinois Tech through the 3+1 Dual Degree UG Programme may be eligible for a merit-based scholarship of up to 25% of tuition fees. At Masters' Union, our dynamic and hands-on pedagogy ensures that each day offers a unique learning experience. With 2-3 classes per day, each spanning 120 minutes, students delve deep into diverse business topics, engaging with expert faculty and their peers in stimulating discussions and practical exercises. Beyond classes, students immerse themselves in a variety of enriching activities throughout the week- CXO Sessions, Industry Practicums, Career Counselling Sessions etc. Can applicants tailor their Masters' Union PGP TBM? Masters' Union offers more than 87 electives, giving students the chance to construct a tailor-made postgraduate program that fits their personal and professional goals. We have new-age, core, and industry concentrations . Students are free to pursue a generalist path toward management or specialise in particular areas by choosing industry concentrations.

Masters' Union offers more than 87 electives, giving students the chance to construct a tailor-made postgraduate program that fits their personal and professional goals. We have new-age, core, and industry concentrations . Students are free to pursue a generalist path toward management or specialise in particular areas by choosing industry concentrations. Regardless of the path students decide to take during their elective terms, everybody graduates with the same PGP TBM certificate with an opportunity to choose industry concentrations. What is the difference between the Flagship PGP TBM program vs the PGP TBM YLC? The content and pedagogy of both PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC remain identical. The PGP TBM Young Leaders Cohort is specifically designed for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience. It follows the same curriculum as the PGP TBM but spans 24 months instead of 16 months. A key highlight of the PGP TBM YLC is a mandatory 3-month internship, offering students practical, real-world exposure to prepare them for leadership roles. Additionally, each core course is taught over 30 hours instead of 20 hours in the PGP TBM. This ensures that students build a strong foundation in critical academic concepts. Are the Scholarships the Same for PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC? Yes, the scholarships available for both the PGP TBM and the PGP TBM YLC are the same. The final grades for most courses will be determined by a mix of class participation, quizzes, simulations, group assignments, projects and exams. Masters' Union grades the exams on a Standard Normal Curve, also called a Z-curve, with a mean of 3.0. There are no forced-to-fails. To graduate, students must maintain a mean grade of 2.1 in both the core and electives courses. What are the benefits of the 16-month programme? The PGP TBM at Masters' Union, with its unique 16-month format, encapsulates the best global practices in management education through a pedagogical approach. Designed to be a fast-paced academic experience, it includes 13 months of rigorous academic training in core areas and industry concentrations with a three-month period of internship and industry immersion, and opportunities to network and seek mentorship. The course is designed for individuals with more than 1 year of work experience.Being in this state of constant engagement gives an opportunity for students to learn how to set priorities and make choices about learning, socialising and personal time from the very beginning of the programme, making them an expert at decision-making, which is one of the most valued qualities in a business leader. What are the benefits of the 24-month PGP TBM YLC programme? The PGP TBM YLC, on the other hand, is specifically crafted for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience and spans 24 months. While the content and pedagogy are identical to the flagship program, the extended timeline allows for deeper learning and gradual development.

While the content and pedagogy are identical to the flagship program, the extended timeline allows for deeper learning and gradual development. Each core course in the PGP TBM YLC is delivered over 30 hours instead of 20, ensuring students build a solid foundation in critical concepts. A key feature of this program is the mandatory three-month internship, which provides students with hands-on industry experience to prepare them for leadership roles. With the additional time and focus on practical exposure, the PGP TBM YLC offers an enriching pathway for early-stage professionals to kickstart their careers with confidence. If an applicant is from a non-tech background, is the Masters' Union a right fit for them? Technology is just one of many skill sets students acquire, alongside business, design, and marketing. Electives allow students to customize their learning, choosing tech-focused courses or exploring other areas like finance, marketing, or entrepreneurship.With practical learning, mentorship, and flexibility, Masters' Union ensures all students, regardless of their background, are prepared for leadership roles in a dynamic business world. The in-person business simulation and interview will be conducted on the same day for a student. These will be scheduled across major cities (Delhi, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Indore, Hyderabad, Chandigarh) in India and over Zoom in exceptional cases. What is GD or business simulation ? How to prepare for it? The in-person business simulation will require students to role-play as a CXO of a company and solve its business challenges in a team of 5-6 applicants. We will send them a case study to prepare for the business simulation round 3-4 days prior for preparation. In this round, they will be judged on their creativity, communication, and teamwork skills. They will be participating in a group discussion for 45 minutes followed by a presentation (without any slides). What happens in the personal interview, what kind of questions will be asked? The interview will be a one-on-one conversation with our faculty or senior leadership. The questions will be around their application and motivations for applying to Masters' Union.

The interview will be a one-on-one conversation with our faculty or senior leadership. The questions will be around their application and motivations for applying to Masters' Union. The goal is to know more about students and what they want to achieve at Masters' Union. Is there any detailed information about GD/PI ? The overall process will take around 3 hours. The business simulation will last 45 minutes followed by a 15 minute group presentation. Students will be working in teams of 4-6 students on a simulated business scenario, where students will be expected to make decisions, analyse data and present their findings. The interview will be conducted by a senior leader or a faculty member at Masters' Union and will be approximately 30 minutes long. They will be asked questions about their application including their achievements, essays and the video essay submitted. Dress code for the event is smart casuals. When will the results be declared? Students can pay the fees semester wise. Starting every semester, they will be notified about the fees due by ugadmissions@mastersunion.org Does Masters' Union offer scholarships? At Masters' Union we believe that financial constraints should not pose any hindrance to students' academic aspirations. We have merit and need-based scholarships for all deserving candidates. Students scoring above 35 out of 45 marks in the Masters' Union Scholarship Aptitude test get a scholarship which can range from 25% - 80% of the tuition fee depending on the student's performance in the Scholarship (Aptitude)Test and the overall profile of the applicant. For candidates keen on scholarship, we encourage students to submit their application early to allow for our admission counsellors to thoroughly review their scholarship case before presenting it to the admissions committee at the time of evaluation. What are the "CA/CFA Pathway" mentioned in the title The curriculum is structured to align with the core content requirements for professional certifications like Chartered Accountant (CA) and Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA). This allows students to simultaneously prepare for these certifications alongside their degree, giving them a significant head start on their professional qualification journey. Is it mandatory to choose a certification (CA or CFA) or sit for the professional exams? No, the decision to sit for the external professional exams (CA or CFA) is entirely optional. The programme is designed to provide the curriculum and preparation necessary for these pathways. However, the choice to pursue the official certification, including registering for and taking the external exams, remains with the student. Your Bachelor's degree from Masters' Union is a stand-alone qualification. When do I need to choose between the CA or the CFA pathway? The decision should be made before the beginning of the course.

Your Bachelor's degree from Masters' Union is a stand-alone qualification. When do I need to choose between the CA or the CFA pathway? The decision should be made before the beginning of the course. We offer dedicated pre-enrollment guidance to help you make an informed choice. Is switching from CA to CFA allowed? Yes, in principle, it is allowed, but the process has two parts: Internal Academic Flexibility (Masters' Union): If a student decides in the first year to switch their focus, then you will not lose the credits from your academic degree. However, we allow case by case basis in the first semester only. External Certification (ICAI/CFA Institute): This is the main point of clarity: you cannot switch credit between the two certification bodies. CA (ICAI) and CFA (CFA Institute) are independent, external qualifications. If you pay the registration fee and clear a level of one (e.g., CA Foundation) and then switch to the other (CFA), you will have to start from Level I of the new certification. The fees paid for the first certification are non-transferable and non-refundable to the new certification. Is switching from CFA to CA allowed? No, this is not allowed given CA has a lot of statutory components and a mandatory articleship. If a student fails a level of the CA or CFA exam, does it affect their degree? No, The UG Programme in Finance & Economics is an independent academic degree.

Is switching from CFA to CA allowed? No, this is not allowed given CA has a lot of statutory components and a mandatory articleship. If a student fails a level of the CA or CFA exam, does it affect their degree? No, The UG Programme in Finance & Economics is an independent academic degree. Your Bachelor's degree is awarded solely based on your successful completion of the required academic coursework, internal exams, and industry projects mandated by Masters' Union. Failure in any level of the professional examinations (CA or CFA) does not affect the student's academic standing or their ability to graduate with the Bachelor's degree from Masters' Union. Are there regular practice tests and mentorship support to track progress? Yes, regular practice tests, detailed assessments, and mock exams are an essential part of the programme to ensure the student is exam-ready. We provide extensive mentorship support to partner on the journey and track progress. What kind of careers can I pursue after completing this programme? Graduates will be prepared for roles across the financial spectrum, including but not limited to: Investment Banking & Equity Research Financial Consulting & Risk Management Wealth Management & Portfolio Management Corporate Finance & Treasury Economic Analysis & Policy Will I graduate with the UG Programme in Finance & Economics and also become a fully qualified CA/CFA Charter Holder at the exact same time (i.e., after 4 years)? No, While the programme is 4 years, the final professional qualification for both CA and CFA will be achieved after you receive your degree. However, we will prepare you for your final level exams for both the qualifications. Is there an option to switch to another Masters' Union UG programme (e.g., Tech & Business Management)?

No, While the programme is 4 years, the final professional qualification for both CA and CFA will be achieved after you receive your degree. Is the business simulation/ personal interview conducted online or offline? The in-person boardroom simulation and interview will be conducted on the same day for a student. At Masters' Union, our dynamic and hands-on pedagogy ensures that each day offers a unique learning experience. With 2-3 classes per day, each spanning 120 minutes, students delve deep into diverse business topics, engaging with expert faculty and their peers in stimulating discussions and practical exercises. Beyond classes, students immerse themselves in a variety of enriching activities throughout the week- CXO Sessions, Industry Practicums, Career Counselling Sessions etc. Can applicants tailor their Masters' Union PGP TBM? Masters' Union offers more than 87 electives, giving students the chance to construct a tailor-made postgraduate program that fits their personal and professional goals. We have new-age, core, and industry concentrations .

Can applicants tailor their Masters' Union PGP TBM? Masters' Union offers more than 87 electives, giving students the chance to construct a tailor-made postgraduate program that fits their personal and professional goals. We have new-age, core, and industry concentrations . Students are free to pursue a generalist path toward management or specialise in particular areas by choosing industry concentrations. Regardless of the path students decide to take during their elective terms, everybody graduates with the same PGP TBM certificate with an opportunity to choose industry concentrations. What is the difference between the Flagship PGP TBM program vs the PGP TBM YLC? The content and pedagogy of both PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC remain identical. The PGP TBM Young Leaders Cohort is specifically designed for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience. It follows the same curriculum as the PGP TBM but spans 24 months instead of 16 months. A key highlight of the PGP TBM YLC is a mandatory 3-month internship, offering students practical, real-world exposure to prepare them for leadership roles. Additionally, each core course is taught over 30 hours instead of 20 hours in the PGP TBM. This ensures that students build a strong foundation in critical academic concepts. Are the Scholarships the Same for PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC? Yes, the scholarships available for both the PGP TBM and the PGP TBM YLC are the same. For detailed information on the scholarship options, please refer to our admissions page. How will applicants be graded at the Masters' Union?

Are the Scholarships the Same for PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC? Yes, the scholarships available for both the PGP TBM and the PGP TBM YLC are the same. For detailed information on the scholarship options, please refer to our admissions page. How will applicants be graded at the Masters' Union? The final grades for most courses will be determined by a mix of class participation, quizzes, simulations, group assignments, projects and exams. Masters' Union grades the exams on a Standard Normal Curve, also called a Z-curve, with a mean of 3.0. There are no forced-to-fails. To graduate, students must maintain a mean grade of 2.1 in both the core and electives courses. What are the benefits of the 16-month programme? The PGP TBM at Masters' Union, with its unique 16-month format, encapsulates the best global practices in management education through a pedagogical approach. Designed to be a fast-paced academic experience, it includes 13 months of rigorous academic training in core areas and industry concentrations with a three-month period of internship and industry immersion, and opportunities to network and seek mentorship. The course is designed for individuals with more than 1 year of work experience.Being in this state of constant engagement gives an opportunity for students to learn how to set priorities and make choices about learning, socialising and personal time from the very beginning of the programme, making them an expert at decision-making, which is one of the most valued qualities in a business leader. What are the benefits of the 24-month PGP TBM YLC programme?

What are the benefits of the 24-month PGP TBM YLC programme? The PGP TBM YLC, on the other hand, is specifically crafted for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience and spans 24 months. While the content and pedagogy are identical to the flagship program, the extended timeline allows for deeper learning and gradual development. Each core course in the PGP TBM YLC is delivered over 30 hours instead of 20, ensuring students build a solid foundation in critical concepts. A key feature of this program is the mandatory three-month internship, which provides students with hands-on industry experience to prepare them for leadership roles. With the additional time and focus on practical exposure, the PGP TBM YLC offers an enriching pathway for early-stage professionals to kickstart their careers with confidence. If an applicant is from a non-tech background, is the Masters' Union a right fit for them? Both the 16-month PGP TBM and the 24-month PGP TBM YLC are designed to seamlessly integrate students from diverse backgrounds, including non-tech fields.While the programs introduce concepts like programming and software design, they remain approachable for those without prior technical expertise. Technology is just one of many skill sets students acquire, alongside business, design, and marketing. Electives allow students to customize their learning, choosing tech-focused courses or exploring other areas like finance, marketing, or entrepreneurship.With practical learning, mentorship, and flexibility, Masters' Union ensures all students, regardless of their background, are prepared for leadership roles in a dynamic business world. Both the PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC attract individuals from diverse academic, professional, and geographical backgrounds.The PGP TBM typically includes professionals with more than 1 year of work experience, while the PGP TBM YLC is tailored for recent graduates or those with 0 1 year of experience. This diversity enriches peer learning and creates a dynamic classroom environment. If an applicant just completed/will be completing their undergraduate studies, is Masters' Union a right fit for them? Work experience is not a mandatory requirement for admission to the PGP TBM YLC. However, for the PGP TBM you must have a minimum 1 year of work experience. All those who will be completing their undergrad degree by May of the following year will be eligible to apply. However, work experience is not mandatory for admission to the PGP TBM YLC, which is designed specifically for freshers and individuals with up to 1 year of experience. If you are dealing with complex family dynamics or need long-term business transformation, leadership growth, and legacy building, OPM is the right choice. It is a 12-month programme for those focused on sustainable growth, succession, and global business exposure. If there are not too many complications in your family dynamics, your primary pain point is sales or business acceleration, and you want to make a shorter commitment of your time, then 9-month BAP is a better program for you. What is the main outcome difference? 12 months OPM = holistic, sustainable transformation and leadership 9 months BAP = fast, practical sales and process gains Will there be the same level of rigour of practical application in both the programs? Yes. Both programs include assignments and Capstone to ensure whatever is taught in the class is thoroughly applied in your company. A pressing problem that your organisation is currently facing is solved with the help of Capstone, with one on one coaching by faculty and mentors. Will I miss out a lot by choosing the BAP? It's all about what your need is. Yes, you will miss out on some aspects like in-depth modules for family, self, patriarch, non family CXOs. Also, international immersions and Fractional Board. Nevertheless, if your current pressing need is revenue growth, then you can go for BAP. Is it worth doing the 12-month program if my goal is only sales growth?

Yes, you will miss out on some aspects like in-depth modules for family, self, patriarch, non family CXOs. Also, international immersions and Fractional Board. Nevertheless, if your current pressing need is revenue growth, then you can go for BAP. Is it worth doing the 12-month program if my goal is only sales growth? It is better to compare all aspects of both programs, what different and additional you are getting in each, and then decide. Can freshers apply for the 9-month BAP Certificate? Not recommended. Ideal for those with at least 2 3 years of business/operations experience. Is the 9-month BAP program also designed for family businesses? Both OPM and BAP are designed keeping needs of family business owners and promoters. Is the 9-month BAP course a subset of OPM? No. It is a different program. While some sessions are similar to OPM, there are many sessions in BAP which are not taught in OPM. See Modules Comparison. Can I switch from OPM to BAP? OPM's first batch with generous scholarships, offer of bringing a family member for free, international immersions, Fractional Board, and almost 2X course modules offers incredible value. Hence, we strongly dissuade students from switching from OPM to BAP. Having completed BAP, can I upgrade myself to OPM by doing additional courses and modules? Yes, it is possible by doing additional modules and international immersions. However, we would like to understand your business objectives and then recommend the best way forward. Can I upgrade from BAP to OPM during the program?

Having completed BAP, can I upgrade myself to OPM by doing additional courses and modules? Yes, it is possible by doing additional modules and international immersions. However, we would like to understand your business objectives and then recommend the best way forward. Can I upgrade from BAP to OPM during the program? Yes, by completing additional modules and paying incremental fees. However, the total cost of upgrading through this pathway will be higher than pursuing OPM directly from the beginning. We recommend carefully evaluating your long term objectives before making this decision. Can I bring a family member or my professional team to the 9-month BAP program? No. This benefit is exclusively available for the first cohort of 12-month OPM. Is the business simulation/ personal interview conducted online or offline? The in-person business simulation and interview will be conducted on the same day for a student. These will be scheduled across major cities (Delhi, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Indore, Hyderabad, Chandigarh) in India and over Zoom in exceptional cases. What is GD or business simulation ? How to prepare for it? The in-person business simulation will require students to role-play as a CXO of a company and solve its business challenges in a team of 5-6 applicants. We will send them a case study to prepare for the business simulation round 3-4 days prior for preparation. In this round, they will be judged on their creativity, communication, and teamwork skills. They will be participating in a group discussion for 45 minutes followed by a presentation (without any slides). What happens in the personal interview, what kind of questions will be asked?

In this round, they will be judged on their creativity, communication, and teamwork skills. They will be participating in a group discussion for 45 minutes followed by a presentation (without any slides). What happens in the personal interview, what kind of questions will be asked? The interview will be a one-on-one conversation with our faculty or senior leadership. The questions will be around their application and motivations for applying to Masters' Union. The goal is to know more about students and what they want to achieve at Masters' Union. Is there any detailed information about GD/PI ? The overall process will take around 3 hours. The business simulation will last 45 minutes followed by a 15 minute group presentation. Students will be working in teams of 4-6 students on a simulated business scenario, where students will be expected to make decisions, analyse data and present their findings. The interview will be conducted by a senior leader or a faculty member at Masters' Union and will be approximately 30 minutes long. They will be asked questions about their application including their achievements, essays and the video essay submitted. Dress code for the event is smart casuals. When will the results be declared? The results are announced 30-45 days after the date of the interview. You can find more details here . Is there a firm deadline for payment of the admission fee? We provide students ample time till July of the academic year so that they can make their decision based on all the admission offers that they have. In case they still want an extension, the same can be granted based on an email request. What is the mode of payment for the fees?

Is there a firm deadline for payment of the admission fee? We provide students ample time till July of the academic year so that they can make their decision based on all the admission offers that they have. In case they still want an extension, the same can be granted based on an email request. What is the mode of payment for the fees? Mode of payment can be online, net banking, bank transfer or in some rare cases they can even send a cheque. Except for cash, we accept all payment methods. What is the fee payment schedule? Students can pay the fees semester wise. Starting every semester, they will be notified about the fees due by ugadmissions@mastersunion.org Is the study abroad programme included in the fee? Is there a different fee? The study abroad programme is not included in the standard tuition fee. Students opting for the 3+1 Dual Degree UG Programme will need to pay tuition fee as per Illinois Tech & living expenses of Chicago. Does Masters' Union offer scholarships? At Masters' Union we believe that financial constraints should not pose any hindrance to students' academic aspirations. We have merit and need-based scholarships for all deserving candidates. Students scoring above 35 out of 45 marks in the Masters' Union Scholarship Aptitude test get a scholarship which can range from 10% - 25% of the tuition fee depending on the student's performance in the Scholarship (Aptitude)Test and the overall profile of the applicant. For candidates keen on scholarship, we encourage students to submit their application early to allow for our admission counsellors to thoroughly review their scholarship case before presenting it to the admissions committee at the time of evaluation.

Is the scholarship for all four years or just for the first year? Scholarship is awarded for all four years. If a student receives a 20% scholarship, they will receive a 20% scholarship every semester on their respective fees. However, in cases of misconduct or rule violations, disciplinary action may be taken. Is the Masters' Union scholarship applicable to the Illinois Tech fee? No, the Masters' Union scholarship is not applicable to the Illinois Tech fee. However, students nominated and admitted to Illinois Tech through the 3+1 Dual Degree UG Programme may be eligible for a merit-based scholarship of up to 25% of tuition fees. To qualify, students must maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0 or higher. The final decision on scholarship awards and eligibility is determined by Illinois Tech in accordance with its admission and scholarship policies. Are there any financing options? Yes, there are financial institutions that can provide loans for up to 95% of the programme fees to the admitted students. Read here for further details. Confirming at the beginning ensures a smooth transition and optimal preparation for their transfer to Illinois Tech. If you are dealing with complex family dynamics or need long-term business transformation, leadership growth, and legacy building, OPM is the right choice. It is a 12-month programme for those focused on sustainable growth, succession, and global business exposure. If there are not too many complications in your family dynamics, your primary pain point is sales or business acceleration, and you want to make a shorter commitment of your time, then 9-month BAP is a better program for you. It is a 12-month programme for those focused on sustainable growth, succession, and global business exposure. If there are not too many complications in your family dynamics, your primary pain point is sales or business acceleration, and you want to make a shorter commitment of your time, then 9-month BAP is a better program for you. What is the main outcome difference? 12 months OPM = holistic, sustainable transformation and leadership 9 months BAP = fast, practical sales and process gains Will there be the same level of rigour of practical application in both the programs? 29 - 34L November 26, 2025 By Pratham Mittal, Founder & CEO, Masters' Union For five years, through bull markets and downturns alike, our PGP cohorts have consistently landed average CTCs between ₹29 34 lakh. People often ask me how it actually happens, especially given that we're still a young institution. Naturally, there's curiosity, and sometimes skepticism. I want to share how we do it, and it's quite different from traditional B-schools. At Masters' Union, placements are methodical, structured, and intensely intentional. Impact of a Dedicated Placement Team We don't rely on student committees to drive placements. Instead, we have a 40-member full-time placement vertical. The team is led by Abhishek Kaul , Anurag Yadav , Nishant Singh , and Simran Bhatia , professionals with corporate experience and exposure to other B-schools. The ratio works out to roughly one team member for every four to five students. In effect, it's almost man-to-man marking. I like to say we run placements like companies run revenue functions. There's no rotating committee, no part-time effort. It's a dedicated, professional engine working to deliver the best outcomes for our students. Running Placements Like Enterprise B2B Sales We operate like a consultative sales organisation. There's a proper pipeline: prospecting mapping meetings farming hunting after-sales. If you have submitted a CAT or GMAT score and are happy with it, then you are not required to take the MU-BAAT. The MU-BAAT is designed to evaluate: Your communication and business aptitude Clarity of thought and idea structuring Creative and analytical thinking You record your responses online and do not need any prior preparation. Think of the questions as a conversation with the Masters' Union team that helps us understand you beyond your r sum . Duration: 45-60 minutes Format: 9 questions divided into 5 sections. At Masters' Union, our dynamic and hands-on pedagogy ensures that each day offers a unique learning experience. With 2-3 classes per day, each spanning 120 minutes, students delve deep into diverse business topics, engaging with expert faculty and their peers in stimulating discussions and practical exercises. Beyond classes, students immerse themselves in a variety of enriching activities throughout the week- CXO Sessions, Industry Practicums, Career Counselling Sessions etc. Can applicants tailor their Masters' Union PGP TBM? Masters' Union offers more than 87 electives, giving students the chance to construct a tailor-made postgraduate program that fits their personal and professional goals. We have new-age, core, and industry concentrations . Students are free to pursue a generalist path toward management or specialise in particular areas by choosing industry concentrations. Regardless of the path students decide to take during their elective terms, everybody graduates with the same PGP TBM certificate with an opportunity to choose industry concentrations. What is the difference between the Flagship PGP TBM program vs the PGP TBM YLC? The content and pedagogy of both PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC remain identical. The PGP TBM Young Leaders Cohort is specifically designed for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience. It follows the same curriculum as the PGP TBM but spans 24 months instead of 16 months. A key highlight of the PGP TBM YLC is a mandatory 3-month internship, offering students practical, real-world exposure to prepare them for leadership roles. Additionally, each core course is taught over 30 hours instead of 20 hours in the PGP TBM. This ensures that students build a strong foundation in critical academic concepts. Are the Scholarships the Same for PGP TBM and PGP TBM YLC? Yes, the scholarships available for both the PGP TBM and the PGP TBM YLC are the same. For detailed information on the scholarship options, please refer to our admissions page. How will applicants be graded at the Masters' Union? The final grades for most courses will be determined by a mix of class participation, quizzes, simulations, group assignments, projects and exams. Masters' Union grades the exams on a Standard Normal Curve, also called a Z-curve, with a mean of 3.0. There are no forced-to-fails. To graduate, students must maintain a mean grade of 2.1 in both the core and electives courses. What are the benefits of the 16-month programme? The PGP TBM at Masters' Union, with its unique 16-month format, encapsulates the best global practices in management education through a pedagogical approach. Designed to be a fast-paced academic experience, it includes 13 months of rigorous academic training in core areas and industry concentrations with a three-month period of internship and industry immersion, and opportunities to network and seek mentorship. The course is designed for individuals with more than 1 year of work experience.Being in this state of constant engagement gives an opportunity for students to learn how to set priorities and make choices about learning, socialising and personal time from the very beginning of the programme, making them an expert at decision-making, which is one of the most valued qualities in a business leader. What are the benefits of the 24-month PGP TBM YLC programme? The PGP TBM YLC, on the other hand, is specifically crafted for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience and spans 24 months. While the content and pedagogy are identical to the flagship program, the extended timeline allows for deeper learning and gradual development.

What are the benefits of the 24-month PGP TBM YLC programme? The PGP TBM YLC, on the other hand, is specifically crafted for individuals with 0 1 year of pre-MBA experience and spans 24 months. While the content and pedagogy are identical to the flagship program, the extended timeline allows for deeper learning and gradual development. Each core course in the PGP TBM YLC is delivered over 30 hours instead of 20, ensuring students build a solid foundation in critical concepts. A key feature of this program is the mandatory three-month internship, which provides students with hands-on industry experience to prepare them for leadership roles. With the additional time and focus on practical exposure, the PGP TBM YLC offers an enriching pathway for early-stage professionals to kickstart their careers with confidence. If an applicant is from a non-tech background, is the Masters' Union a right fit for them? Both the 16-month PGP TBM and the 24-month PGP TBM YLC are designed to seamlessly integrate students from diverse backgrounds, including non-tech fields.While the programs introduce concepts like programming and software design, they remain approachable for those without prior technical expertise. Technology is just one of many skill sets students acquire, alongside business, design, and marketing. Electives allow students to customize their learning, choosing tech-focused courses or exploring other areas like finance, marketing, or entrepreneurship.With practical learning, mentorship, and flexibility, Masters' Union ensures all students, regardless of their background, are prepared for leadership roles in a dynamic business world.
